newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-RUBIN DEFEATS FRAZIER AT EVERT CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUBIN DEFEATS FRAZIER AT EVERT CUP.

text.p: Fifteenth
seed Chanda Rubin outlasted fellow American Amy Frazier 6-3
4-6 7-6 (8-6) in a marathon first-round match Friday at the
$1.25 million State Farm Evert Cup.
All five seeds in action on the opening day -- Rubin, 16th
seed Lisa Raymond, 12th-seeded Elena Likhovtseva of Russia,
13th-seeded Nathalie Tauziat of France and 14th-seeded
Ruxandra Dragomir of Romania -- won their matches.
The top eight seeds all received first-round byes.
Spaniards Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and Conchita Martinez are
the unexpected top two seeds, injuries having forced Steffi
Graf, Monica Seles and Mary Pierce to withdraw.
Two youngsters who have received international attention
-- 15-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova and 16-year-old
American Venus Williams -- were also in action Friday.
The 89th-ranked Kournikova defeated 60th-ranked tour
veteran Patricia Hy-Boulais of Canada 1-6 6-1 6-4.
A qualifier into the main draw, the 211th-ranked Williams
posted an easy 6-2 6-4 win over 48th-ranked Anne Miller.
The two hour, 32 minute match between the 25th-ranked
Rubin and 31st-ranked Frazier saw both players have difficulty
asserting themselves through three sets as tedious to play as
to observe.
Of the 255 points played, more than half were ended by
unforced errors. Rubin posted 70 unforced errors while Frazier
was only slightly better with 67.
Rubin scored only 26 overall winners and Frazier just 22.
"It definitely wasn't my best match," said Rubin, who won
her first career title earlier this year in Linz, Austria.
"I felt a little bit more pressure from her than against
someone who doesn't hit the ball so hard. I should've taken
some pace off the ball. It should've been a much easier match
then I made it."
Break point opportunities were plentiful. Rubin won 11 of
22 service break chances, while Frazier took advantage of 10
of 23.
"For the most part, my serve was not good, especially at
the end of the second and for all of the third set," said
Rubin, who sat out most of 1996 with a wrist injury. "I lost
most of my service games."
